newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sets up U.S. hotline for Holocaust claims.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sets up U.S. hotline for Holocaust claims.

text.p: Germany's Allianz AG Holding, one of the insurers named in a multi-billion-dollar U.S. lawsuit alleging Holocaust survivors were cheated of their assets, said on Tuesday it had opened a hotline in the U.S. to assist claimants.
A spokesman for the top German insurer said claimants in the U.S. could call the toll-free number 1 800 411 0118 while claimants outside the U.S. could call the collect number 001 416 205 4653.
Information will be given in English, Spanish and Hebrew, Allianz said. The U.S. numbers can be dialled from Wednesday at 1300 GMT or 0900 New York time, the spokesman said.
The insurer last week set up a 24-hour hotline in Germany under +49 89 41864 413.
Allianz last week detailed steps it had taken to clarify issues from the Nazi era and pledged to answer queries as quickly and completely as possible.
A lawsuit filed late last month charges seven European insurers with concealing or converting the cash value and proceeds of insurance policies sold prior to 1946 to victims of Nazi persecution.

The class action suit, combining the claims of an estimated 10,000 plaintiffs, said insurers had earlier encouraged Europeans fearing persecution to deposit assets with them and buy insurance to safeguard their families' futures.

Allianz has pledged to examine any outstanding claims and deal with them with minimum red tape but has also said it does not expect many cases to be uncovered. Auditing firm Arthur Andersen is to conduct an independent examination of its files.

Other defendants in the U.S. case include Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A. of Trieste, Italy, Wiener Allianz Versicherungs AG and Der Anker Allgemeine Versicherungs AG of Vienna, A.G.F. Assurances Generales de France Vie of Paris, Riunione Adriatica Di Sicurta S.p.A. of Milan and Bavarian Reinsurance Co of Munich.
